context:
Billboard JAPAN

＜訪談＞目標新時代——
Hololive 所屬
虛擬偶像星街彗星高歌「革命」之音樂

Part 1

採訪：Takuto Ueda

Hololive 所屬的 VTuber／虛擬偶像  星街彗星  推出了全新專輯《新星目錄》。

這是繼前作《Specter》後，睽違約兩年的第三張專輯，並以「革命」作為關鍵詞，是一張充滿挑戰性的作品。收錄了包含氣勢如虹的 VOCALOID 製作人ツミキ所提供的歌曲《ビビデバ》，該曲也成為星街彗星首支累計串流播放量突破 1 億次的歌曲。此外，專輯還集結了山内總一郎（フジファブリック）、川谷繪音（indigo la End、極品下流少女等）、Deu（PEOPLE 1）、なとり、春野等多位風格多元且實力強勁的創作者，共同創作了 11 首樂曲。而專輯的壓軸曲《綺麗事》中，星街彗星也首次挑戰了作詞與作曲。

從出道以來，星街彗星不斷創造「VTuber 史上首次」的成就。「希望 VTuber 更加融入社會」這是她多年來的心願。懷抱著追求新時代的堅定意志，她攜手第三張專輯，並將於 2 月 1 日登上夢想的舞台——日本武道館，舉行個人演唱會。在這個重大的轉折點來臨之際，她回顧了專輯的製作過程，並分享了對自身活動的想法。

               對我來說的革命

——首先從年末的話題開始說起。參與【COUNTDOWN JAPAN 24/25】的舞台感受如何？

星街：這場演出跟我自己的演唱會不同，現場有許多可能不認識我的人，但他們依然非常熱情，讓我感到非常高興。我和樂團成員還說「我們大幹了一場呢」，演出結束後我也自搜了網上的評價，有人留言說「雖然以前只聽過名字，但這場演出真的很棒」。

——尤其是在您出演的最後一天，除了常見的搖滾樂團外，SixTONES 和 NewJeans 等多元的陣容也非常吸引人。觀眾群體應該相當廣泛，您是怎麼考慮如何展現自我的呢？

星街：雖然作為 VTuber 是虛擬的存在，但其實我們也是和大家一樣的「人」，我覺得這次可能成功地讓觀眾感受到這一點。另外，演出前我也進行了公開彩排。

——這確實是音樂節特有的形式呢。

星街：我還認真帶動了現場的應援互動，也努力讓大家感受到我們的熱情。

——考慮到這場演出緊接著巡演，是否也因此狀態調整得更好呢？

星街：是的，因為巡演剛好在三個地點舉行了演出，累積了經驗，所以能帶著「好，衝吧！」的心情參加這次活動。如果去年完全沒有演唱會經驗，我可能會非常緊張，但因為巡演結束後我的狀態非常好，這次也能以良好的熱情投入其中。

——經歷了這樣的年末活動後，您推出了備受期待的新專輯《新星目錄》。您的首張專輯主打「彗星般閃耀的明星原石」，展現了偶像般閃亮的新鮮感；第二張專輯則將活動中的煩惱和掙扎昇華為作品。那麼，第三張專輯對您來說是怎樣的一張作品呢？

星街：我們團隊對專輯的風格有簡單的定義，第一張是「閃亮」，第二張是「閃耀」。接下來我們討論第三張時，決定「那就爆炸吧！」於是出現了「創造新時代」的概念，並以「革命」作為主題。作為虛擬藝術家，目前我們在社會中還是一個異質的存在，還未被視為真正的人。但我想表達的是，我們是真正在唱歌、跳舞的，而這就是我心中的革命。因此，專輯中收錄了許多表達這種目標的歌曲。

——從「閃亮」、「閃耀」到「爆發」。武道館公演的主題也是“SuperNova（超新星）”。至於專輯名中的「目錄」，是否帶有某種自我介紹的意涵？

星街：原本我們計劃只用「新星」這個詞，但當我們看到 Mika Pikazo 老師設計的專輯封面時，覺得畫作非常美，我們想在不妨礙設計的情況下加上文字，於是決定放在四角，並加入了「目錄」這個詞。雖然當時並沒有特別深的含義，但之後大家給出了很多很棒的解讀，那就這麼定了（笑）。

——也就是說，專輯名稱是在最後才決定的？

星街：沒錯，是在收到封面設計之後才定下來的。不過「新星」這個詞是我從一開始就想使用的。

——您過去在配信和訪談中多次提到：「希望 VTuber 能更廣泛地被社會接受，所以自己也會不斷挑戰。」這次更是將這一理念明確作為主題進行創作。您在製作過程中具體考慮了哪些方面呢？

星街：在第二張專輯中，我已經展現了不少鬱結、混沌的情感，但我希望在此基礎上進一步進化。所以在第二次個人演唱會結束後，我開始思考如何展現更加進化的樣子。這個階段就是要展現新的挑戰與突破，我認為現在正是這樣的階段。

Billboard JAPAN

<Interview> Aiming for a New Era—
Hololive Virtual Idol Hoshimachi Suisei Sings
“Revolution” in Her Music

January 2025

Interviewed by : Takuto Ueda

Hoshimachi Suisei, a VTuber and virtual idol under Hololive, has released her new album,《Shinsei Mokuroku》.

This is her third album and her first in about two years since her previous work, 《Specter》. The album is an ambitious project centered around the keyword “revolution.” It includes 11 tracks created by a diverse and talented lineup of creators, such as the rising VOCALOID producer Tsumiki, whose track “Bibbidiba” became her first to surpass 100 million total streams. Other contributors include Soichiro Yamauchi (Fujifabric), Enon Kawatani (indigo la End, Gesu no Kiwami Otome, etc.), Deu (PEOPLE 1), Natori, and Haruno. Hoshimachi Suisei herself takes on songwriting and composition for the first time with the closing track, “Kireigoto”.

Hoshimachi Suisei has achieved numerous “Firsts” in VTuber history. With a long-held desire to make VTubers more recognized in society, she has poured her determination to forge a new era into this third album. On February 1st, she will fulfill her dream of holding a solo concert at Japan’s iconic Nippon Budokan. On the brink of this major turning point, she reflects on the album’s creation process and shares her thoughts on her career.

         My Revolution

—Let’s start with your recent performance at 【COUNTDOWN JAPAN 24/25】. How was the experience?

Hoshimachi: Unlike my own live shows, I imagine there were a lot of people in the audience who didn’t know me, but the energy was amazing, and I was really happy. My band members and I even said to each other, “We nailed it!” After the performance, I checked social media and saw comments like, “I only knew her name, but that was great!”

—Especially on the final day of the festival, the lineup was quite diverse, featuring regular rock bands alongside SixTONES and NewJeans. The audience must have been very diversified. How did you plan to present yourself?

Hoshimachi: Although I’m a VTuber and exist in a virtual space, I wanted to convey that I’m just like everyone else—a human being. I think I managed to achieve that. They even let me do an open rehearsal before the main show.

—That’s a very festival-like feature.

Hoshimachi: I made sure to encourage call-and-response interactions and tried to create a real sense of shared energy.

—Coming right after your tour, your condition must have been well-prepared for this performance, correct?

Hoshimachi: Yes, since I had just completed a three-show tour, I had the experience under my belt and felt like, “Let’s do this!” If I hadn’t done any live shows last year, I probably would have been super nervous. But coming off the tour, I could bring great energy into this performance.

—After such a busy year-end, you’ve now released your much-anticipated new album, Shinsei Mokuroku. With your debut album emphasizing the “fresh, sparkly feeling of a shooting star” and your second album expressing struggles and emotions through your activities, how would you describe this third album?

Hoshimachi: Within the team, we referred to the first album as “sparkle,” the second as “shiny,” and for the third, we thought, “What’s next? How about an explosion?” From there, the concept evolved into “let’s create a new era,” leading to the theme of “revolution.” As a virtual artist, I feel like we’re still seen as an unusual presence in society—not entirely recognized as human. But the fact is, I sing and dance myself, and making people understand that is my revolution. That’s the kind of message I aimed to deliver through this album.

—From “sparkle” to “shine” to an “explosion.” The title of your Budokan performance, “SuperNova,” fits perfectly with that progression. As for the term “Mokuroku” (Catalogue) in the album title, does it carry a self-introductory nuance?

Hoshimachi: Initially, we were just going to use “Shinsei” (Nova), but Mika Pikazo-sensei’s jacket illustration was so beautiful that I wanted to add some text in a way that wouldn’t interfere with the artwork. That’s how “Mokuroku” (Catalogue) was added. It didn’t have a deep meaning at first, but since people have interpreted it in such wonderful ways, I’ll go with that (laughs).

—So the title was finalized just last minute?

Hoshimachi: Yes, after the jacket art arrived. I was always determined to use the term “Shinsei” (Nova), though.

—In past streams and interviews, you’ve frequently mentioned your desire for VTubers to gain wider societal acceptance and your commitment to taking on challenges to achieve that. This time, you’ve made it the direct theme of your album. What were your specific thoughts during the production process?

Hoshimachi: With my second album, I showed a lot of darker, more turbulent emotions. But after that, I felt like I needed to close that chapter and show a more evolved version of myself. Around the time my second solo concert ended, I started thinking about how to demonstrate that growth. I realized it was time to showcase new challenges and breakthroughs—this album is about that next phase.
